answer: Epoch-Linked Behavioural Continuity Rule. Each identity's cross-epoch state commits to a rolling fingerprint of its prior interactions (timing, counterparties, content hashes). Any new identity must inherit a continuity chain; breaks trigger re-entry at a throttled tier with a nectar of withheld rewards held for N epochs. To forge fresh identities at scale, an attacker must generate plausible historical behaviour for each one, paying per-identity compute and time that compounds across the river of epochs, making farms linear-cost rather than free.
